question: Who designed the 'first' small computer for home use?
solution:
The correct answer is __**John Blankenbaker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• John Blankenbaker designed the first small computer intended for home use, known as the **Kenbak-1**.
 
• The Kenbak-1 was introduced in 1971 and is considered one of the first personal computers.
 
• It used discrete transistor logic and had 256 bytes of memory.
 
• The Kenbak-1 was advertised for $750 and was primarily used for educational purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chuck Peddle**

 
 
• Chuck Peddle was an influential engineer who developed the MOS Technology 6502 microprocessor.
 
• The 6502 was used in several early personal computers, including the Apple I and II, Commodore PET, and Atari 8-bit family.
 
 
 
• **Steve Wozniak**
 
 
• Steve Wozniak is a co-founder of Apple Inc. and the designer of the Apple I and Apple II computers.
 
• The Apple II, launched in 1977, was one of the first highly successful mass-produced personal computers.
 
 
 
• **Steve Leininger**
 
 
• Steve Leininger was an engineer at Tandy Corporation who co-designed the TRS-80, one of the first mass-produced personal computers.
 
• The TRS-80 was introduced in 1977 and was one of the best-selling personal computers of its time.
 
 
 
• **John Blankenbaker**
 
 
• John Blankenbaker is credited with designing the Kenbak-1, which is considered the first commercially available personal computer.
 
• The Kenbak-1 was a simple machine that used switches and lights for input and output.
